# Modeq

> Modeq is a transparent, consensus-verified content moderation registry built on GenLayer Intelligent Contracts. Instead of a single company's model deciding what gets moderated, five GenLayer validators independently classify each submission and a majority must agree; a deterministic threshold - not the model - turns that classification into ALLOW, FLAG, or BLOCK, and every case is written to a public, on-chain audit log.

## What it does

- Accepts a piece of text and classifies it against a fixed category set (spam, hate speech, harassment, nsfw, violence, none) using an LLM running independently on multiple GenLayer validators.
- The model returns structured categories and a confidence score only - it never states a final verdict. Fixed Python thresholds in the Intelligent Contract compute ALLOW / FLAG / BLOCK deterministically.
- Every case (text, categories, confidence, decision) is stored on-chain and is publicly listable, with no wallet required to read it.

## Pages

- / - product landing page and explanation of the consensus mechanism
- /app - submit text for moderation (requires a MetaMask-compatible wallet on GenLayer)
- /audit - public, read-only audit log of every case ever submitted
- /demo - 77-second narrated walkthrough of the live app, with chapters and captions

## Live deployments

- GenLayer Studio (primary demo network)
- GenLayer Asimov testnet
- GenLayer Bradbury testnet

## Underlying technology

Built on GenLayer Intelligent Contracts (Python, GenVM runtime). Consensus uses a custom `gl.vm.run_nondet_unsafe` leader and validator pair: each validator re-runs the classification independently and a verdict is written on-chain only when the validators agree on the decision and the primary category. The frontend is a Next.js app talking to the contract through genlayer-js.
